title: One company, five names.
dek: The same customer lives in your inbox, your ledger and your CRM under different names. Every report quietly disagrees, and nobody can say why.
summary: The same customer is "HSC" in the inbox, a vendor ID in the ledger and a different record in the CRM. Every report quietly disagrees, and nobody can say why.
alt: A wall of numbered grey mailboxes
caption: Every box has a number. None of them know who lives there.
linkedin:
Ask a simple question: how much did we do with our biggest supplier last year?

Finance has one number.
Sales has another.
Operations remembers a third.

All three people are right. All three numbers are wrong.

The problem isn't the math. That supplier isn't one thing in your systems. It's five.

Full note in the comments.

The diagram shows how one company becomes five.

In the ledger it's vendor 10423. In the CRM it's "Harbor Supply Co." In the inbox it's "HSC." The payment processor has a customer ID. The spreadsheet calls it "Harbor (old acct)."

No record is a mistake. Each system named it the way that system needed.

The fix isn't renaming everything. It's giving every name somewhere to point.

A quick test you can run Monday:

1. Pick your five most important customers or suppliers.
2. Search for each one in every system you use: ledger, CRM, inbox, payments, the spreadsheet.
3. Write down every name, number and nickname you find.

If any of them has more than two, every report that combines those systems is quietly disagreeing with itself.

Question for finance and operations leaders:

Who in your organization is the person who knows that "HSC" and vendor 10423 are the same company?

What happens when they're on vacation?
